_about: Each in-scope query paraphrases the subject of one patent's abstract/title (as extracted in data/processed/txt), mostly avoiding the title's exact wording, and is labeled with that patent as relevant.
Queries of type 'lay_language' deliberately use everyday wording that differs from the patent text (vocabulary mismatch), to test meaning-based matching rather than shared keywords.
Patent families with near-identical content (US8332207/US8812291 and US9037464/US9740680) list both members as relevant.

Labels are single-annotator and were drafted with AI assistance while preparing the project for review; they should be reviewed by the project owner. Other patents may also be partially relevant to a query; this set only measures whether the target patent is found.
Out-of-scope queries have no relevant patent in the corpus and are used to calibrate the relevance threshold.
